results.name: What’s embroidery backing?
results.title: What’s embroidery backing?
results.body:
Embroidery backing is a supportive layer added to fabric during embroidery. It stabilizes the material and gives the stitches a strong surface to hold onto. This keeps your design looking sharp and helps it last over time.

Because different fabrics behave differently during embroidery, we use various types of backing based on the product material and design placement.

Types of embroidery backing we use

Tear-away backing

This is a lightweight backing that’s easy to remove. After embroidery, the extra backing is torn away, leaving just a bit inside the design to keep it stable.

Used for:

  • Dad hats
  • Lightly structured snapbacks
  • Baseball caps
  • Bucket hats
  • Tote bags
  • Hoodies
  • Other items made from thicker fabrics

Cut-away backing

This type is thicker and sturdier. It’s designed for delicate or stretchy fabrics that need extra support. After embroidery, the extra backing is trimmed around the edges, leaving a small ¼″ (3–6 mm) border.

We also add a layer of tear-away backing underneath for even more stability. This helps prevent stitches from sinking into soft or elastic fabrics.

  • Used for:
  • T-shirts
  • Beanies
  • Thin or stretchy materials

No backing

Some products, such as backpacks or structured snapback front panels, are made from thick, firm materials that don’t need any extra support during embroidery.

What backing colors do we use?

To help the backing blend in with the garment, we choose colors based on fabric type:

  • White backing for light garments and all headwear that requires only a tear-away backing
  • Black backing for dark garments
  • Semi-transparent backing for t-shirts, especially white or lightweight fabric, to reduce visibility

Embroidery backing may not be visible on the outside, but it plays a key role in making your design look great and last longer.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: Are all products in an order shipped together?
results.title: Are all products in an order shipped together?
results.body:
Not always. Some items are packaged separately to keep them safe and in good shape during shipping. Others might be sent from different fulfillment centers, so they’ll arrive in separate packages.

Here are some products we often ship separately:

  • Structured hats
  • Backpacks
  • Mugs, wine tumblers, and pint glasses
  • Postcards and stickers
  • Pillows
  • Posters
  • Framed posters
  • Canvas prints
  • Water bottles
  • Notebooks
  • Blankets
  • Other outsourced products

If your order has different types of products, it’s normal to receive them in multiple shipments.

Note
We recommend calculating the shipping fees for the product categories mentioned here, assuming that they would always ship separately. Occasionally, some of these products can be shipped together with other products, but they would still be charged as a single product for the shipping fee.

results.name: How are your products packaged?
results.title: How are your products packaged?
results.body:
We package every order with care to make sure your products arrive safely. Depending on the item and where it’s going, we use materials like paper or plastic mailers, cardboard boxes, and protective inserts such as foam pouches or bubble wrap when needed.

All apparel orders shipped from our in-house facilities now use post-consumer recycled (PCR) plastic bags. In North America, where most of our merchants and customers are located, we’ve fully switched to packaging with 90–100% PCR plastic content.

Common packaging materials

  • Poly mailers (white or grey): Made from at least 70% PCR plastic.
  • Clear inside bags: At least 30% PCR, used to group multiple items.
  • Cardboard boxes: Used for fragile or larger items.
  • Eco mailers in Australia: Compostable mailers with clear composting instructions.
  • Bubble envelopes: Used for specific products like notebooks and pin button sets.
  • Stay-flat envelopes: Provide extra support for flat items like posters and stickers.
Note
PCR plastics come from recycled everyday items like plastic bags and wrapping film.

Product-specific packaging

Apparel & textiles

  • Packaged in PCR poly mailers.
  • For multi-item orders, each item is placed in a clear inner bag before being put into the mailer. Single-item orders are placed directly in the mailer without the inner bag.
  • Australia: Shipped in compostable eco mailers.
  • Japan and China: Packed in standard plastic mailers.

Hats

  • Structured hats: Shipped in cardboard boxes.
  • Beanies: Shipped like other apparel in PCR mailers.

Home & living

  • Textiles (blankets, towels, etc.): In PCR poly mailers.
  • Large or multi-item orders: In cardboard boxes.
  • Mugs, bottles: In brown cardboard boxes.
  • Jigsaw puzzles: Puzzle pieces are stored in a black storage box with the puzzle image on top, then shipped in a cardboard box. Orders with more than two puzzles are split into shipments with one or two puzzles per shipment.
  • Pet bowls: In brown cardboard boxes. Details may vary depending on fulfillment location. 
  • Yoga mats: Shipped in cardboard boxes.

Stationery

  • Stickers: Kraft envelopes or plastic bags with stay-flat inserts.
  • Greeting cards/postcards: Kraft envelopes.
  • Journals: Flat paper mailers.
  • Notebooks: Shipped in cardboard boxes or packaged in bubble envelopes.

Wall art

  • Framed posters/canvases: Cardboard boxes (sizes from 12 × 18 × 2 to 28 × 38 × 6 inches), wrapped in tissue paper and bubble wrap or foam.
  • Posters: Triangular kraft boxes (no plastic caps) or stay-flat envelopes for smaller sizes (like 8 × 10 inches).
  • Australia: Posters shipped in triangle tube boxes.

Other decor

  • Metal prints: Cardboard boxes.
  • Pin buttons:
    • Single items: Paper mailers.
    • Sets: Bubble mailers.
  • Magnets: Paper mailers.
  • Wooden ornaments: Shipped in a white mailing envelope with a PP (polypropylene) inner bag.

Tech accessories

  • Phone cases (tough & snap): Each case is packed in a separate, smaller cardboard box.
  • AirPods® cases (rubber): Each case in its own smaller cardboard box.
  • AirPods® cases (others): Padded paper mailers with an extra internal pouch.
  • Desk mat: Rolled up in a poly bag. For orders of more than 10 items, they’re laid flat and shipped in a cardboard box.

Our packaging choices focus on protecting your products, reducing environmental impact, and using the best locally available materials.

Want to boost your brand with custom mailers? Learn how to use your own packaging to create a standout unboxing experience.

results.name: Why Etsy shipping rates may not match Printful flat rates?
results.title: Why Etsy shipping rates may not match Printful flat rates?
results.body:
When you connect your Etsy shop to Printful, Flat‑Rate shipping profiles are automatically pushed to your Etsy listings. These rates reflect the cost Printful charges you based on product types and destinations. However, Etsy uses a different shipping calculation logic, which can lead to two types of mismatches:

  • Variant-level mismatch: Etsy applies one shipping profile per listing, so all variants share the same rate—even if their actual shipping costs differ.
  • Multi-item shipment mismatch: Etsy assumes items in an order ship together, while some Printful products are fulfilled and shipped separately.

Variant-level shipping limitation on Etsy

Etsy shipping profiles apply to the entire listing, not to individual product variants. This creates a limitation when your Printful product includes variants with different shipping costs.

When a product is synced to Etsy, Printful automatically assigns a single flat-rate shipping profile to the listing. If the variants within that product have different shipping rates (for example, different sizes), we apply the shipping profile with the highest shipping cost to ensure your expenses are covered.

This means:

  • All variants in the listing will display the same shipping price on Etsy
  • That price will reflect the most expensive variant’s shipping rate

Example:

If you publish a poster with multiple sizes (e.g., 8×10" and 24×36"):

  • The 24×36" size has a higher shipping cost, so its rate is applied to the entire listing
  • A customer purchasing the 8×10" variant will still be charged the higher 24×36" shipping rate on Etsy
  • Printful will charge you the actual shipping cost for the 8×10" variant

As a result, customers may be overcharged for shipping on smaller or lighter variants.

What you can do:

  • Separate variants with significantly different shipping costs into individual listings
  • Consider offering free shipping and incorporating the cost into your retail price

Which products ship separately

Some Printful items arrive in their own packages to protect their shape and ensure safe delivery. Etsy isn’t aware of this and may undercharge shipping because it treats everything as a single shipment. The following products ship separately:

  • Structured hats (snapback, baseball, trucker)
  • Backpacks
  • Mugs, wine tumblers, pint glasses
  • Posters (regular & framed), canvases
  • Stickers, postcards, notebooks
  • Pillows with stuffing
  • Water bottles, bean bags, blankets

How Printful calculates shipping

Printful uses flat-rate pricing based on:

  1. Shipping category (e.g., shirts, mugs, hats)
  2. Order contents:
    • If items ship together (same category), we charge a “first-item” rate plus “additional-item” rates.
    • If items ship separately (different categories or separate packaging), we charge full “first-item” rates for each product. 

Learn more about this here

Why shipping on Etsy may appear too low

Etsy’s system calculates shipping based on the highest “first-item” rate plus “additional-item” rates for other products in the order. It has no awareness of separate shipments. That mismatch means Etsy’s shipping might not cover what Printful charges you.

Example: Shipping a t-shirt, mug, and stickers to the U.S.

  • What Printful charges you:

    Each item ships separately, so you’re charged for each one’s first-item rate.

    • T-shirt: $3.99
    • Mug: $6.99
    • Stickers: $3.25
      Total: $14.23

  • What Etsy charges the customer:

    Etsy charges based on one highest first-item rate and lower additional-item rates.

    • Mug (highest first item): $6.99
    • T-shirt (additional item): $1.25
    • Stickers (additional item): $0.05
      Total: $8.29

Protect your profits on Etsy

To avoid losing money, consider these actions:

  • Make sure your retail prices cover those extra shipping costs
  • Watch orders carefully, especially when customers buy separately shipped items
  • Consider free shipping, rolling in all shipping costs to simplify the pricing strategy

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: How do I set up a TikTok Shop account?
results.title: How do I set up a TikTok Shop account?
results.body:
Thinking about selling on TikTok Shop? We’ll walk you through account creation, identity verification, and payment setup; everything you need to start selling in the US or UK.

Log in with your existing TikTok account, or register a new one here for the US and here for the UK, using a phone number or email address. Once registered, you’ll verify your identity, upload your bank info for payouts, and you’re ready to start selling.

Step 1: Create your TikTok Shop account

  1. Go to TikTok Shop Seller Center, then sign in or register using your TikTok account, email, or phone.
  2. Select your shop region (US or UK) and click Enter.
  3. Choose a seller type: Individual or Business.
  4. Confirm eligibility; you must be at least 18 years old and a legal resident in your selected market.

Step 2: Set up warehouse & return addresses

  1. Navigate to Logistics → Warehouses in Seller Center.
  2. Enter the full Warehouse Address using the appropriate Printful facility address (not a P.O. box), including the street address, postcode, your name as the contact person, and your phone number. TikTok requires a physical address for fulfillment, so make sure to use Printful’s facility in your selling region.
  3. Optionally, set a Return Warehouse Address or mark the pickup address as the return address by checking Set as return address.
  4. Agree to the terms and click Start Your Business.

Step 3: Submit identity verification documents

  1. After address setup, submit verification documents:
  • Individual sellers: upload government-issued photo ID (passport, driver’s license, or national ID). Both front and back may be required. Documents must be clear, valid, and in accepted formats (JPEG, PNG, or PDF under 10 MB). Your ID name must match your account and bank details exactly.
  • Business sellers: upload a government-issued ID for the legal representative plus official business documentation (certificate of incorporation, business license, or equivalent). These must include the legal business name, address, business type, and tax ID or legal identifier (such as EIN in the U.S.).
  1. Click Submit; approval typically takes 24–48 hours, occasionally up to 72 hours. 

Step 4: Link your bank account

Once your documents are approved:

  1. Go to the Seller Center homepage and click Link Bank Account.
    • For individuals: use a personal bank account matching your verified name.
    • For businesses: use a business account matching the registered company name.
  2. Provide account name, bank name, account number, address, and email, then click Submit, and wait for confirmation.

Step 5:  Connect your TikTok video account (recommended)

Link your TikTok Official Account to ensure your Shop appears on your TikTok profile:

  1. In Seller Center, go to My Account → Linked Accounts.
  2. Click Link, scan the QR code via the TikTok mobile app, review and approve terms, and finish the linking process.

Once linked and products are approved, your “Shop” tab will appear in your TikTok profile and video bio.

Step 6: Connect your TikTok Shop to Printful

Now that your TikTok Shop is set up, go to your Printful Dashboard → Stores → Choose platform → Click Connect under TikTok. Or follow this link to go directly to the connection page.

Final steps

  • Double-check that all names and information across documents, the TikTok account, and the bank account match perfectly.
  • Once approved, you can start pushing products; ensure product listings meet TikTok’s guidelines (e.g., required title length).
  • When your store is active, connect your Printful account and begin listing products for fulfillment.

Why meeting these requirements matters

  • Identity and account verification protect your account - TikTok reviews personal and bank information carefully to prevent fraud and comply with regulations.
  • Accurate documentation ensures the payout process and maintains account health.
  • Inconsistencies or missing information can delay approval or block your ability to sell.

Learn more about getting started with TikTok

  • How do I set up my US tax information on TikTok?
  • How do I set up shipping for TikTok?
  • Do I need to authorize the Printful app for TikTok Shop?
  • What happens if my TikTok Shop account gets suspended?

results.name: How can I duplicate designs in Printful’s Design Maker?
results.title: How can I duplicate designs in Printful’s Design Maker?
results.body:
Duplicating your design layers is a great way to create quick variations or maintain a consistent look across different parts of a product. Whether you need an identical copy on the same side or want to move a design from the front to the back, the Design Maker allows you to do so in just a few clicks.

Duplicate a layer

To make a copy of any design layer:

  1. Go to the Layers panel on the right.
  2. Select the layer you want to copy.
  3. Click the three-dot menu next to the layer.
  4. Choose Duplicate.

A copy of the layer will appear directly above the original, and you can adjust it however you like.

Duplicate to other print areas

For All-Over Print (AOP) products with multiple placement areas (like sleeves, front, and back), you can easily copy your layer to another section.

  1. Select the layer you want to duplicate.
  2. Click the arrow next to the Duplicate button.
  3. Choose the print area where you want the copied layer to appear.

This makes it easy to keep your design consistent across multiple placements.

results.name: Why am I unable to reship my returned items?
results.title: Why am I unable to reship my returned items?
results.body:
To ensure every item we ship meets our quality and hygiene standards, we do not restock or reship all returned products. While we hold most returned items for 30 days, any product that is not in resellable condition will be removed from stock and won't be available for reshipment.

Which items are ineligible for reshipment?

Items that have been opened or worn—specifically apparel like underwear, swimsuits, or baby bodysuits—cannot be reshipped. Because these items may come into contact with bodily fluids, we prioritize the health and safety of our customers by not putting them back into stock. Additionally, any returns that appear worn, used, or damaged during our inspection process will not be eligible for reshipment.

Note
Some carriers may dispose of returns during transit, so not all returns make it back to us.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: What is Printful's return and refund policy?
results.title: What is Printful's return and refund policy?
results.body:
Since every Printful product is made to order, we don't accept returns or exchanges for buyer's remorse, wrong size, or wrong color. If an order arrives damaged, defective, or misprinted, you can request a free reshipment or a refund; there is no need to send the item back.

Note
You must report any quality issue or lost package within 30 days of the delivery date (or the estimated delivery date, for packages that never arrived). Claims submitted after that window can't be honored.

What's covered under Printful's refund policy

You're eligible for a free reshipment or refund if:

  • The product arrived damaged or defective (for example, a manufacturing error, warped print, or ink issue).
  • The design was misprinted (wrong placement, wrong colors, wrong item).
  • The package was lost in transit.

For quality issues, you'll need to provide a clear photo of the affected product. If several items with the same design are affected, include one photo showing all of them together.

What's not covered under Printful's refund policy

We don't offer a reshipment or refund if:

  • The customer ordered the wrong size or color.
  • The customer changed their mind after receiving the order.
  • The customer entered the wrong shipping address (in this case, a reshipment can be arranged, but reshipping costs apply).

Exception: For orders shipped to Brazil, customers have the legal right to cancel their order within 7 calendar days of receiving it, under the “right to regret” policy. If this applies, please contact us via the contact form or start a chat.

How to submit a refund or reshipment claim

You can request a reshipment or refund from your Printful Dashboard or by contacting our Support Team. Make sure to describe the issue and attach a clear photo (or video, if multiple items are affected). For a full walkthrough on how to report a problem, please visit the article: How do I report a problem with my order? 

Our team reviews each report and lets you know whether it's approved.

How refunds are issued

By default, approved refunds are deposited into your Printful Wallet, where you can use them toward future orders or withdraw them back to your original payment method. 

If you sell through Quick Stores or submitted your order without creating an account, the refund goes directly to the original payment method instead.

What happens to returned packages

If a package is returned to our facility (for example, due to an invalid address), you'll get an email notification. You can then arrange a reshipment. Shipping charges will apply if the order was unclaimed at customs, returned by the customer, or an incorrect address was provided.

If you don't claim a returned item within 30 days, it's donated to charity and can no longer be reshipped.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: Why are my mockups not updating on my Squarespace storefront?
results.title: Why are my mockups not updating on my Squarespace storefront?
results.body:
If you’ve updated your product design in Printful but not all the mockups are displaying the changes on your Squarespace storefront, don’t worry; there's a common and easily resolvable reason for this.

What’s happening?

When you add a product with multiple color options (like black and white) from Printful to your Squarespace store, Printful automatically assigns only one mockup per color variant to represent it.

If you added extra mockups during product setup, for example, lifestyle images or alternate angles, they will still show up in your Squarespace storefront. However, they are not linked to specific color variants, and won’t automatically update if you change the product design later.

Example

  • You push a t-shirt to Squarespace with:
    • Two color variants: black and white
    • Two mockups for each color (front and back)
  • What Printful does:
    • Assigns one mockup to the black t-shirt variant (e.g., front view)
    • Assigns one mockup to the white t-shirt variant (e.g., front view)
    • The other mockups (e.g., back views) are displayed on your storefront, but not tied to a specific color
  • Later, if you update the design in Printful:
    • Only the mockups directly assigned to each variant (the front views) will update
    • The back-view images remain unchanged unless manually updated

How to fix it

To get all your product images up to date:

  1. Go to your Squarespace Dashboard
  2. Navigate to Commerce → Inventory
  3. Click the product you want to update
  4. Add or replace images manually for each variant

This ensures all mockups reflect your latest design, no matter how many you’ve uploaded originally.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: Does the new, larger embroidery area of the hat front panel change anything for me?
results.title: Does the new, larger embroidery area of the hat front panel change anything for me?
results.body:
Yes, and it’s good news! A larger embroidery area means more room for your designs, giving you even more creative freedom. This update affects a growing list of hats, and we’ve made it easy for you to take advantage of the new space, whether you’re using existing designs or creating something new. 

Which hats now have the larger embroidery area?

The front embroidery space on these high-profile hats has increased from 5.5″ × 2″ (13.97 × 5.08 cm) to 6.3″ × 2.56″ (16 × 6.5 cm):

  • Snapback | Otto Cap 125-978
  • Flat Bill Cap | Yupoong 6007
  • Foam Trucker Hat | Otto Cap 39-165
  • 5 Panel Trucker Cap | Yupoong 6006
  • Classic Snapback | Yupoong 6089M

The front embroidery space on these low-profile hats has increased from 5.5″ × 2″ (13.97 × 5.08 cm) to 5.9″ × 2″ (15 × 5.08 cm):

  • Closed-Back Trucker Cap | Flexfit 6511
  • Snapback Trucker Cap | Richardson 112
  • Camouflage Trucker Hat | Otto Cap 105-1247

The front embroidery space on these low-profile hats has increased from 4″ × 1.75″ (10.16 × 4.45 cm) to 5.9″ × 2″ (15 × 5.08 cm):

  • Retro Trucker Hat | Yupoong 6606
  • Closed-Back Structured Cap | Flexfit 6277
  • adidas Dad Hat

The front embroidery space on these low-profile hats has increased from 4″ × 1.75″ (10.16 × 4.45 cm) to 5.5″ × 2″ (13.97 × 5.08 cm):

  • Vintage Corduroy Cap | Big Accessories BA703
  • Organic Baseball Cap | Econscious EC7000
  • Classic Dad Hat | Yupoong 6245CM
  • Vintage Cap | Otto Cap 18-1248
  • Distressed Dad Hat | Otto Cap 104-1018
  • Denim Hat | Otto Cap 18-204
  • Tie-Dye Hat | Sportsman SP400
  • Pastel Baseball Hat | Beechfield B653

More styles may be added in the future as we continue to expand the selection.

Can I reuse my existing designs?

Yes, you can freely resize or move your existing designs to fit the new embroidery area without incurring any additional charges. You only need to pay the standard digitization fee if you rotate the design or add new elements.

Will I be charged again if I use an existing design on the larger area?

No extra fees as long as you’re just resizing or repositioning. Since rotation or adding new elements requires fresh digitization, you would then be charged, but simple scaling or shifting doesn’t cost anything extra.

Can I still use the original, smaller embroidery area?

Absolutely. If you’ve already saved or synced a product template with the original 5.5" × 2" placement, you can continue using it. But when you start a new hat design now, the larger area is the default.

Can I use both standard and unlimited embroidery with the new placement?

Yes, just like before, you can choose either standard or unlimited embroidery for the larger area.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: Can I share Printful’s address with my customers?
results.title: Can I share Printful’s address with my customers?
results.body:
You are welcome to share Printful’s address with your customers for return purposes, though there are a few important things to keep in mind.

If you display our address on your website, we recommend adding a disclaimer stating it is only for product returns. We also suggest asking customers to contact you before sending anything back. This allows you to guide them through the process and ensures our Support Team can assist more efficiently if needed. To understand the full process, please review our Return policy.

Return address format

When using our address for returns, please format it as: 

[Your Store Name] Returns 
[Printful return address] 

You can find the full list of our return addresses here. 

What not to use our address for

Don’t use our address for: 

  • Legal correspondence.
  • Your business’s legal address.
  • General letters or documents not related to a return. 

We’re not legally permitted to open correspondence that isn’t addressed to us directly, so these types of mail will be returned to the sender.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: How do I report a problem with my order?
results.title: How do I report a problem with my order?
results.body:
If there's an issue with your order, submit a problem report from your Printful Dashboard. This creates a support ticket, and our team reviews it along with any photos you attach.

Note
Submit your problem report within 30 days of the delivery date, or the estimated delivery date if the order never arrived. We aren't able to accept reports filed after this timeframe.

What can I report as a problem with my order?

Submit a problem report if the order arrived damaged, misprinted, or defective, if you received the wrong item or size, if part of the order is missing, or if more than 5 business days have passed since the estimated delivery date and the order still hasn't arrived.

How do I submit a Problem Report?

Step 1: Open the affected order

  1. Log in to your Printful account.
  2. Go to your Orders page and find the order (you can search using the order number).
  3. Open the order.
  4. Click Report problem at the bottom of the order view to open the problem report form.

If you don't see the Report problem button, the order is either outside the 30-day window or hasn't reached a status where a report can be filed. Contact our Support Team with the order number, and we'll check it for you.

Step 2: Choose the topic

Select the type of problem and your preferred solution.

Step 3: Describe the issue and submit it

Describe the issue in detail for each affected item and upload photos where relevant. Including clear images with your initial report avoids a back-and-forth that delays resolution. See What photos to submit when reporting a problem for the specifics on what we need to see.

Click Report problem to send your request.

What happens after I submit a problem report?

We review the report and reply through the ticket. If we need more information, such as an additional photo, we'll ask for it in that reply, so the report stays open until we hear back from you.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.

results.name: Why was my order canceled?
results.title: Why was my order canceled?
results.body:
In rare cases, your order or shipment may be canceled by our Support team. This can happen for several reasons, such as a product being discontinued or out of stock, a payment or security concern, or an order addressed to a destination we're unable to ship to (see Are there any shipping restrictions? for details). 

If this happens, the funds used to pay for the order will be returned to your Printful Wallet. If the order was placed anonymously, without a registered Printful account, the refund will instead go back to the original payment method used at checkout.

Order canceled automatically after a hold

Not every cancellation comes directly from our Support team reviewing your order. If your order was placed on hold and the underlying issue wasn't resolved within 30 days, it's automatically canceled and refunded to your Printful Wallet — or to the original payment method if the order was placed without a registered account. To understand why orders get placed on hold in the first place, and how to resolve a hold before it leads to a cancellation, see Why is my order on hold?

Most of the time, your order would first be placed on hold to allow you to review and resolve any issues. However, if your order was canceled without being put on hold, you can find the reason by following these steps:

  1. Go to your Printful Dashboard
  2. Navigate to Orders
  3. Click on the specific order
  4. Click on the Holds and order history tab
  5. There, you'll see details about the cancellation

This tab shows a full timeline of status changes for the order, including any holds, cancellations, or other updates our team has made, so it's a good first stop any time an order's status looks different than expected.

Reordering a canceled order

If you'd like to place that same order again, you don't need to rebuild it entirely from scratch. From your Orders tab, filter by Canceled, open the order you want to resubmit, and select Copy order. This creates a new draft with all the original order details already filled in, which you can review, adjust if needed, and submit again. Since product pricing, stock, and file requirements can change over time, it's worth double-checking the new draft carefully rather than assuming everything will match the original order exactly. See Why is my order on hold for the full walkthrough of this process.

  • If your refund went to your Wallet, it doesn't require any action on your part — you can leave the balance there to cover future orders, or withdraw it from Dashboard → Billing → Printful Wallet → Withdraw. 
  • If it went to your original payment method instead, no further steps are needed; it'll simply appear back on that account.

Still need help? Our Support Team is here for you—reach out anytime through our contact form or start a chat with us.
